source_ref: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066 (PLOS ONE 20(4):e0321066, CC BY 4.0; Measurement section, and Table 2 image at /article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066.t002); S1 Data workbook https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066.s001; processing script data/jiang_2025_empathy.py
note: BLOCKED -- no item wording is published for any of the seven items, and the code->item mapping cannot be established by any route. The IRW table holds empathy1..empathy7 (240 responses each, resp 2-7); data/jiang_2025_empathy.py melts the S1 Data workbook's own columns of those names, so the code IS the source column name -- but that name carries no text. The deposit is a single XLSX (S1 Data, 10.1371/journal.pone.0321066.s001, one sheet '480样本-英文 loc 2024.3.11', 240 rows x 48 columns) whose header row is bare codes (ID, sentiments1-5, attitudes1-5, concerns1-5, PL1-2, EI1-2, ITE1-6, CE1-6, BME1-6, empathy1-7, gender, education, level); there are no variable or value labels of any kind, and S1 Data is the article's ONLY supplementary file. The PLOS ONE article (CC BY 4.0) names the instrument -- 'the empathy dimension of Davis's (1996) Interpersonal Response Indicator Questionnaire ... seven question items on a 7-point scale, ranging from 1 to 7, representing complete disagreement to complete agreement' -- and quotes exactly ONE example sentence ('I often feel soft and caring toward those less fortunate than me', the study's own rendering of IRI Empathic Concern item 2) without saying which code it is. Its tables are images and were fetched and read rather than assumed (t001, t002 via the article/figure/image endpoint): Table 2 lists Empathy1..Empathy7 with factor loadings only (0.824-0.916, alpha 0.949, CR 0.958, AVE 0.766) and no wording; no other table reproduces items. So the seven canonical IRI Empathic Concern statements (IRI items 2, 4R, 9, 14R, 18R, 20, 22) are known, but which of them is empathy1 is not, and nothing in the data distinguishes them: item means are 5.39-5.56 (all seven within 0.17, SDs 0.93-0.98), every inter-item correlation is positive and large (r = 0.65-0.88), and all seven share one 7-point range (six span 3-7, empathy7 spans 2-7) -- so Step 5b routes 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 have no purchase and all 5040 assignments remain equally consistent with every available fact. Route 6 is worse than silent: the canonical EC subscale has three reverse-worded items, and the uniformly positive correlation matrix means the deposit either stores them already reversed or the Chinese adaptation reworded them -- so canonical wording shipped against this table's 1=disagree..7=agree anchors would be inverted for three unidentifiable items, breaking the option_text<->resp axis as well as item_text<->item. LANGUAGE: administration was Chinese (Heze University pre-service teachers; the paper states the English instruments were translated into Chinese and back-translated), and no Chinese wording exists in scope -- the XLSX holds no CJK outside its sheet name and the article prints none -- so even a shipped table would have been the English fallback. RIGHTS: not the reason for the block; Davis's IRI carries no quotable fee or no-redistribution clause found, and the article is CC BY 4.0. No __items.csv written; per Step 5b a blocked table has no live item text and so carries no mapping_verification row and no verify_jiang_2025_empathy.R. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. Every source was retrieved successfully (article HTML, S1 XLSX, table images); the source simply never published the item wording or the code->item key. It would flip only if the authors deposited the administered Chinese questionnaire with its item codes, or published per-item statistics for empathy1..7 that could be matched against item_stats.R output. SIBLINGS: jiang_2025_sacie, jiang_2025_inclusive_efficacy and jiang_2025_teaching_motivation come from this same workbook and face the identical header-with-no-labels situation; no file belonging to any of them was created, edited or read for writing.

source_ref: PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0321066 (CC BY 4.0) + S1 Data .s001 XLSX; instrument: Sharma, Loreman & Forlin (2012) TEIP, as revised in Chinese by Li Y (2018), Northwest Normal University master's thesis (CNKI, gated); data/jiang_2025_inclusive_efficacy.py
note: BLOCKED -- no item wording exists in any source IRW can reach, and the item codes cannot be tied to the canonical instrument beyond subscale membership. (1) Source: Jiang N, Li H, Ju SY, Kong LK, Li J (2025) PLoS ONE 20(4):e0321066 (CC BY 4.0). Its only supporting file is S1 Data (.s001 XLSX, one sheet '480 samples-English loc 2024.3.11'), whose header row is bare codes -- ID, sentiments1..5, attitudes1..5, concerns1..5, PL1, PL2, EI1, EI2, ITE1..6, CE1..6, BME1..6, empathy1..7, gender, education, level -- with no variable labels, no second header row and no codebook sheet. data/jiang_2025_inclusive_efficacy.py melts those columns by name, so the IRW item code IS the source column name (core model 3, pattern 1); nothing is positional, and nothing is labelled. (2) The article body reproduces no item wording: the Measures section names the instrument only ('Teachers' Efficacy of Inclusive Education Practices Scale developed by Sharma, et al. in 2012 and revised by Chinese researcher, Li (2018) ... 18 questions ... three elements: inclusive teaching efficacy (ITE), collaborative efficacy (CE), and behavioral management efficacy (BME) ... 6-point Likert scale from 1-6'). Both table images were fetched and read (t001 = respondent demographics, t002 = the PLS-SEM measurement model: construct, indicator code, factor loading, alpha, CR, AVE) -- neither prints an item stem. Grep of the full article text for TEIP item phrases returns nothing. (3) The administered wording is Chinese (240 Chinese pre-service teachers) and comes from a REVISION, Li Y (2018) master's thesis, Northwest Normal University, available only via CNKI (kns.cnki.net, subscription-gated); it is in neither the deposit nor the paper's supplements, so under the recoverability scope it is unrecoverable. (4) The English TEIP wording is openly published, but it cannot be mapped: the canonical TEIP numbers its 18 items 1-18 with the three factors INTERLEAVED, not blocked (e.g. item 3 'I can make parents feel comfortable coming to school' is collaboration, item 5 'I can accurately gauge student comprehension' is instruction, item 8 'I can control disruptive behavior in the classroom' is behaviour management). ITE1..6 / CE1..6 / BME1..6 are therefore a within-factor RENUMBERING of a non-contiguous set, done by a Chinese revision whose ordering nobody publishes; 720 assignments per subscale are equally consistent with everything available. No Step 5b route separates them: all 18 items share the same 1-6 scale (route 2 dead), subscale membership is already given by the code prefix so block structure tests nothing new (route 5 dead), the paper publishes no per-item M/SD/floor/ceiling and no subscale totals (routes 1 and 3 dead), the codes are not self-describing, and per-item means from a foreign-language validation sample would not discriminate 6 near-collinear items of one facet. Only the subscale is recoverable, and the subscale is already in the code, so no defensible item_text can be written. No __items.csv was written.

source_ref: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066 (PLOS ONE 20(4):e0321066, CC BY 4.0; Measurement section and Table 2 image at /article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066.t002); S1 Data workbook https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0321066.s001 ; instrument wording: Forlin C, Earle C, Loreman T, Sharma U (2011), Exceptionality Education International 21(3):50-65, https://ojs.lib.uwo.ca/index.php/eei/article/view/7682 (doi 10.5206/eei.v21i3.7682), Appendix; processing script data/jiang_2025_sacie.py
note: BLOCKED on two independent grounds; no __items.csv written. (1) RIGHTS -- the only publication of the canonical English SACIE-R wording that could be located is CC BY-NC. The 15 items are printed in full in the Appendix of Forlin, Earle, Loreman & Sharma (2011), Exceptionality Education International 21(3), and that journal's own article page states: "Authors retain copyright and grant the journal right of first publication with the work simultaneously licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial License that allows others to share the work for non-commercial purposes with an acknowledgement of the work's authorship and initial publication in this journal." (https://ojs.lib.uwo.ca/index.php/eei/article/view/7682, fetched 2026-09-07). Under references/itemtext_standard.md the licence of the source IRW actually copied from governs, and a CC BY-NC source does not ship -- the chinvararak_2021_ecr shape exactly. The Jiang PLOS article is CC BY 4.0 but publishes no item wording, so it cannot be the source. Search for a permissively licensed reproduction was systematic and came up empty: Europe PMC full-text search on the canonical item strings ("Students who are inattentive should be in regular classes", "Students who need an individualized academic program should be in regular classes", "I dread the thought that I could eventually end up with a disability", "I would feel terrible if I had a disability", "I tend to make contacts with people with disabilities brief", "I find it difficult to overcome my initial shock when meeting people with severe", "I am afraid to look directly at a person with a disability") returned 0-1 hits each and none reproduces the scale; all 15 open-access Europe PMC hits for SACIE were listed and the three that mention 'regular classes' (PMC8277994, PMC13067759, PMC12563666) quote at most one item or a 12-item Spanish adaptation back-translated into English, not the canonical 15. (2) MAPPING -- independent of rights, and fatal on its own. The IRW codes are sentiments1-5, attitudes1-5, concerns1-5; data/jiang_2025_sacie.py melts the S1 workbook's own columns of exactly those names, so the code IS the source column name (core model 3, pattern 1), but that name carries no text: the workbook is a single sheet ('480 samples-English loc 2024.3.11', 240 rows x 48 columns) whose header row is bare codes with no variable labels, no value labels, no second header row and no codebook sheet, and S1 Data is the article's ONLY supporting file. The canonical SACIE-R numbers its 15 items 1-15 with the three dimensions INTERLEAVED (sentiments = canonical items 2, 5, 9, 11, 13; attitudes = 3, 6, 8, 12, 15; concerns = 1, 4, 7, 10, 14), so sentimentsN/attitudesN/concernsN are a within-dimension RENUMBERING of a non-contiguous set that nobody publishes. Which canonical statement is 'sentiments1' is not recoverable, and nothing in the data separates the 5!^3 = 1,728,000 candidate assignments: computed from the S1 workbook, all 15 item means fall in 4.00-4.25 (SDs 1.06-1.18, n=240 each), within-dimension inter-item r is uniformly 0.64-0.74 with no outlier, all 15 items share one 1-6 response range, and the paper's Table 2 gives per-indicator PLS loadings only (Sentiments1-5 = .860/.853/.855/.850/.842; Concerns1-5 = .876/.844/.850/.844/.831; all within .045) with no wording attached. Step 5b routes 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 therefore have no purchase, and route 6 is dead too because every item within a dimension shares one polarity. (3) A THIRD problem the wording would have carried: the paper states "The higher questionnaire scores indicating more positive attitudes", and in the data all three dimensions intercorrelate POSITIVELY (sentiments-concerns r = 0.23-0.42, sentiments-attitudes 0.18-0.32, attitudes-concerns 0.26-0.37), which for a scale whose sentiments and concerns items are all negatively worded means those 10 items are stored ALREADY REVERSED. Canonical 1=strongly disagree..6=strongly agree anchors shipped against them would have been inverted for 10 of 15 items, breaking the option_text<->resp axis as well. (4) LANGUAGE: administration was Chinese (240 Chinese pre-service teachers, Heze University). The paper states the questionnaire "was initially adapted from an English language version, which was then translated into Chinese by translator ... The study also employed a bilingual English lecturer from Heze university for back translation". No Chinese wording exists in scope -- the XLSX holds no CJK outside its sheet name and the article prints none -- so even had the rights and mapping been resolved, the table would only have been an English translated_substitute. (5) Step 3b instrument check PASSED before the block: the table really is the SACIE-R. The Measurement section states "This study used the Scale of Sentiments, Attitudes, and Concerns about Inclusive Education (SACIE-R), a 15-question scale revised by Forlin et al. (2011) ... attitudes (5 questions), concerns (5 questions), and sentiments (5 questions) ... 6-point Likert scale from 1-6", and the live table matches exactly: 15 items, 5 per named dimension, n=240 each, 3,600 rows, resp set {1,2,3,4,5,6}. (6) Per Step 5b a blocked table has no live item text and so carries no mapping_verification row and no verify_jiang_2025_sacie.R; a header-only verification_jiang_2025_sacie.csv is written with a NO_ROUTE row recording that the check was attempted, following the batch_057 sibling precedent. (7) RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate. Every source was retrieved successfully (article HTML, S1 XLSX, both table images, the EEI PDF); nothing timed out, 403'd or hit a quota. The block would flip only if a NEW source appeared: a CC BY / CC0 publication reproducing the canonical 15 English SACIE-R items, or the authors depositing their administered Chinese questionnaire with its item codes. Note the duboz_2021_swls precedent -- a licence block that turns on which page the words came from is reopenable if a permissive page is later found, so this is a licence verdict on the sources that exist today, not a permanent exclusion. (8) SIBLINGS: jiang_2024_instituinteg, jiang_2024_ptsacc, jiang_2025_empathy and jiang_2025_inclusive_efficacy are owned by other agents this round; no file belonging to any of them was created, edited or deleted here.

note: mapping_basis=paper_explicit and it is VERIFIED against the data. The live codes are 'Item Moral 1'..'Item Moral 9' -- data/jimenezherrera_2022_moral_sensitivity.py melts the S1 xlsx by column name (var_name='item'), so the IRW code IS the source column header, but that header is a bare number and carries no text; the S1 workbook has one sheet, a single header row of column names and no variable or value labels of any kind (checked with openpyxl), so level-1 data labels do not exist here. The wording comes from the paper's own Table 1, 'Lexical and semantic equivalence of the MSQ-SPV', which prints every item as 'Item k' / 'Item k' in parallel English and Spanish columns -- an explicit code-to-text tie by number, not an order inference. Table 1 is an IMAGE (no HTML endpoint; grep over the scraped article text returns nothing), so it was fetched via journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=...t001 and read directly; the transcription is OCR-by-reading and is worth a human spot-check. Deviations from literal transcription, all deliberate: the 'Item k.' / 'Item k.' prefixes were stripped from every stem; the paper's English item 6 begins 'II find it very difficult' and the doubled 'I' was corrected to 'I'; item 7's Spanish sentence is printed with no closing period in the source and is shipped that way. item_text = the administered Spanish (language=Spanish); item_text_translated = the paper's English column, which is Lutzen's ORIGINAL English MSQ rather than a rendering of the adapted Spanish -- hence translation_source=official_instrument_english. The two columns diverge by design in items 3, 7 and 9: the paper states 'the term "to feel" was replaced by the term "to know" (saber) in item 3 and the term "balance" was replaced by the term "possibility" (posibilidad) in item 7', and the Spanish item 3 asks about knowing whether and when to tell a patient the truth while the English asks about talking about difficult things. This is disclosed in public_note. instructions and section_prompt are blank: neither the paper nor the deposit publishes administered instructions, and there is no testlet structure (one trivial section_id). option_text is blank for every level -- no Spanish anchor labels are published anywhere in scope; the only anchor information is the paper's English prose, 'it has nine items or assumptions with six possible answers, where the value 1 means absolute disagreement with the statement and 6 complete agreements', so those two endpoint descriptions are carried in option_text_translated for resp 1 and 6 only and the four unlabelled interior points are left blank rather than padded with their own numbers. Step 3b: the table name, the dictionary description and the live data agree -- 9 items, resp 1-6, n=751, matching the paper's MSQ-SPV exactly (Item Moral 7 uses only 5 of the 6 levels); the study administered no second instrument that could be confused with it. Rights: the wording ships from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article that printed it in full; no fee and no redistribution or use clause for Lutzen's MSQ could be found or quoted (the literature records permission obtained by personal communication to ADMINISTER translations, which is not a quotable bar on redistribution), so silence-is-permission applies.
public_note: The English in the _translated columns is the original English wording of Lutzen's Moral Sensitivity Questionnaire, printed by the paper beside its Spanish adaptation rather than translated from it, so it diverges from the administered Spanish in items 3, 7 and 9 (the authors replaced "to feel" with "to know" in item 3 and "balance" with "possibility" in item 7); the Spanish item_text is what respondents actually read, and it was transcribed from an image of the paper's Table 1
